response.reason: NL1 establishes a cardinality/region-structure obligation (three regions in this diagram). The owner is ActiveState because it is the composite that structurally contains and encloses these three regions; NL1's phrase 'this diagram' at the top level maps to the entire collision-avoidance sub-machine, whose composite realization is ActiveState.

response.reason: This lens examines contract completeness/structure across NL1 (cardinality), NL2 (initial-entry/derived event-consumer-coverage), and NL3 (region-structure/derived state_action). Cross-view facts show: (1) the FCSTM ActiveState has three concurrent regions (FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion) matching NL1's count-3 requirement, so cardinality binding is exact with member_domain=concurrent_regions. (2) NL2's initial-entry contract requires the collision-avoidance sub-machine (ActiveState) to be entered from its enclosing owner (root/InitialState) upon the three named events; the exact source inventory and FCSTM show InitialState -> ActiveState triggered by 'Collision Detected', which is a single combined event, not the three named ones (frontend/rear-end/pedestrian collision events) — those events instead fire only inside ActiveState.Inactive after ActiveState is already active. This is a structural mismatch: the three-event disjunction that the owner should react to for activation is not implemented as the actual owner-level entry trigger; instead a single generic 'Collision Detected' event activates the sub-machine, and the three specific events are consumed only internally by an already-active Inactive state. This exposes a contrastive inconsistency between NL2's stated activation triggers and the actual owner-level transition group. (3) NL3's region-structure obligation is satisfied by the FCSTM's three regions but with no separator syntax being required beyond existence — structurally the three states exist as concurrent regions within ActiveState, satisfying region_structure requirement, so omitted from candidates. However each region's exit edge (BrakingControl/SteeringControl/EmergencyStop -> [*]) transitions to Inactive gated by a guard on shared variable R45RouteToken, which is a compiler-macro-encoded exit; these guards are macro artifacts not directly NL violations. (4) The derived event-consumer-coverage contract (NL2-DERIVED) requires each of the three collision events to be an accepted activation trigger of the sub-machine at the owner scope; but structurally, none of the three actually triggers entry into ActiveState from the owner (root/InitialState) -- only 'Collision Detected' does. This is a genuine structural/contrastive gap: the group NL-GROUP-NL2-ACTIVATION's three alternatives (frontend/rear-end/pedestrian) have no matching owner-level transition_endpoints at all; the owner only has one generic trigger. This grounds a wrong-target/missing structural mismatch for the transition group and supports the initial_entry contract's violation, plus the event-consumer-coverage derived contract violation.

output.reason: This lens examines contract completeness/structure across NL1 (cardinality), NL2 (initial-entry/derived event-consumer-coverage), and NL3 (region-structure/derived state_action). Cross-view facts show: (1) the FCSTM ActiveState has three concurrent regions (FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion) matching NL1's count-3 requirement, so cardinality binding is exact with member_domain=concurrent_regions. (2) NL2's initial-entry contract requires the collision-avoidance sub-machine (ActiveState) to be entered from its enclosing owner (root/InitialState) upon the three named events; the exact source inventory and FCSTM show InitialState -> ActiveState triggered by 'Collision Detected', which is a single combined event, not the three named ones (frontend/rear-end/pedestrian collision events) — those events instead fire only inside ActiveState.Inactive after ActiveState is already active. This is a structural mismatch: the three-event disjunction that the owner should react to for activation is not implemented as the actual owner-level entry trigger; instead a single generic 'Collision Detected' event activates the sub-machine, and the three specific events are consumed only internally by an already-active Inactive state. This exposes a contrastive inconsistency between NL2's stated activation triggers and the actual owner-level transition group. (3) NL3's region-structure obligation is satisfied by the FCSTM's three regions but with no separator syntax being required beyond existence — structurally the three states exist as concurrent regions within ActiveState, satisfying region_structure requirement, so omitted from candidates. However each region's exit edge (BrakingControl/SteeringControl/EmergencyStop -> [*]) transitions to Inactive gated by a guard on shared variable R45RouteToken, which is a compiler-macro-encoded exit; these guards are macro artifacts not directly NL violations. (4) The derived event-consumer-coverage contract (NL2-DERIVED) requires each of the three collision events to be an accepted activation trigger of the sub-machine at the owner scope; but structurally, none of the three actually triggers entry into ActiveState from the owner (root/InitialState) -- only 'Collision Detected' does. This is a genuine structural/contrastive gap: the group NL-GROUP-NL2-ACTIVATION's three alternatives (frontend/rear-end/pedestrian) have no matching owner-level transition_endpoints at all; the owner only has one generic trigger. This grounds a wrong-target/missing structural mismatch for the transition group and supports the initial_entry contract's violation, plus the event-consumer-coverage derived contract violation.

result.reason: This lens examines contract completeness/structure across NL1 (cardinality), NL2 (initial-entry/derived event-consumer-coverage), and NL3 (region-structure/derived state_action). Cross-view facts show: (1) the FCSTM ActiveState has three concurrent regions (FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion) matching NL1's count-3 requirement, so cardinality binding is exact with member_domain=concurrent_regions. (2) NL2's initial-entry contract requires the collision-avoidance sub-machine (ActiveState) to be entered from its enclosing owner (root/InitialState) upon the three named events; the exact source inventory and FCSTM show InitialState -> ActiveState triggered by 'Collision Detected', which is a single combined event, not the three named ones (frontend/rear-end/pedestrian collision events) — those events instead fire only inside ActiveState.Inactive after ActiveState is already active. This is a structural mismatch: the three-event disjunction that the owner should react to for activation is not implemented as the actual owner-level entry trigger; instead a single generic 'Collision Detected' event activates the sub-machine, and the three specific events are consumed only internally by an already-active Inactive state. This exposes a contrastive inconsistency between NL2's stated activation triggers and the actual owner-level transition group. (3) NL3's region-structure obligation is satisfied by the FCSTM's three regions but with no separator syntax being required beyond existence — structurally the three states exist as concurrent regions within ActiveState, satisfying region_structure requirement, so omitted from candidates. However each region's exit edge (BrakingControl/SteeringControl/EmergencyStop -> [*]) transitions to Inactive gated by a guard on shared variable R45RouteToken, which is a compiler-macro-encoded exit; these guards are macro artifacts not directly NL violations. (4) The derived event-consumer-coverage contract (NL2-DERIVED) requires each of the three collision events to be an accepted activation trigger of the sub-machine at the owner scope; but structurally, none of the three actually triggers entry into ActiveState from the owner (root/InitialState) -- only 'Collision Detected' does. This is a genuine structural/contrastive gap: the group NL-GROUP-NL2-ACTIVATION's three alternatives (frontend/rear-end/pedestrian) have no matching owner-level transition_endpoints at all; the owner only has one generic trigger. This grounds a wrong-target/missing structural mismatch for the transition group and supports the initial_entry contract's violation, plus the event-consumer-coverage derived contract violation.

response.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, and stable termination/dead-end frontier facts. The closed FCSTM shows the three collision-avoidance regions (FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion) and their internal states (BrakingControl, SteeringControl, EmergencyStop) are structurally present but entirely unreachable from the root because ActiveState's only initial edge targets Inactive, and Inactive's outgoing transitions (Frontend_Collision_Detected, Rear_End_Collision_Detected, Pedestrian_Collision_Detected) target leaf states FrontendCollision/RearEndCollision/PedestrianCollision that have zero outgoing transitions rather than entering the corresponding regions. This breaks: (1) the NL2 initial-entry/activation contract - the named collision events do not actually activate/enter the sub-machine's operative collision-handling behavior (the regions), (2) the derived NL2 event-consumer-coverage contract - Collision_Avoided has consumers but none reachable, and the named detection events lead only to dead-end leaves, not into the actual mitigation regions, (3) the NL3 region-structure/state-action contract - the orthogonal regions can never become active so "concurrent activation of different collision avoidance controls" cannot occur. These are three independent behavioral defects sharing one deterministic root cause (STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL / EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE / LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING), which I keep as one candidate per distinct contract per the instructions, using repeated facts in each candidate's basis. Cardinality contract (NL1, three regions) is handled via cardinality_bindings only, no candidate. Region-structure contract (NL3) is a structural/existence property (the three regions do exist as concurrent siblings under ActiveState) so it is satisfied structurally; I instead route the operational-consequence failure to the derived state_action contract (NL3-DERIVED) and to NL2's contracts, avoiding duplicate candidates for the same structural fact.

output.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, and stable termination/dead-end frontier facts. The closed FCSTM shows the three collision-avoidance regions (FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion) and their internal states (BrakingControl, SteeringControl, EmergencyStop) are structurally present but entirely unreachable from the root because ActiveState's only initial edge targets Inactive, and Inactive's outgoing transitions (Frontend_Collision_Detected, Rear_End_Collision_Detected, Pedestrian_Collision_Detected) target leaf states FrontendCollision/RearEndCollision/PedestrianCollision that have zero outgoing transitions rather than entering the corresponding regions. This breaks: (1) the NL2 initial-entry/activation contract - the named collision events do not actually activate/enter the sub-machine's operative collision-handling behavior (the regions), (2) the derived NL2 event-consumer-coverage contract - Collision_Avoided has consumers but none reachable, and the named detection events lead only to dead-end leaves, not into the actual mitigation regions, (3) the NL3 region-structure/state-action contract - the orthogonal regions can never become active so "concurrent activation of different collision avoidance controls" cannot occur. These are three independent behavioral defects sharing one deterministic root cause (STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL / EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE / LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING), which I keep as one candidate per distinct contract per the instructions, using repeated facts in each candidate's basis. Cardinality contract (NL1, three regions) is handled via cardinality_bindings only, no candidate. Region-structure contract (NL3) is a structural/existence property (the three regions do exist as concurrent siblings under ActiveState) so it is satisfied structurally; I instead route the operational-consequence failure to the derived state_action contract (NL3-DERIVED) and to NL2's contracts, avoiding duplicate candidates for the same structural fact.

result.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, and stable termination/dead-end frontier facts. The closed FCSTM shows the three collision-avoidance regions (FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion) and their internal states (BrakingControl, SteeringControl, EmergencyStop) are structurally present but entirely unreachable from the root because ActiveState's only initial edge targets Inactive, and Inactive's outgoing transitions (Frontend_Collision_Detected, Rear_End_Collision_Detected, Pedestrian_Collision_Detected) target leaf states FrontendCollision/RearEndCollision/PedestrianCollision that have zero outgoing transitions rather than entering the corresponding regions. This breaks: (1) the NL2 initial-entry/activation contract - the named collision events do not actually activate/enter the sub-machine's operative collision-handling behavior (the regions), (2) the derived NL2 event-consumer-coverage contract - Collision_Avoided has consumers but none reachable, and the named detection events lead only to dead-end leaves, not into the actual mitigation regions, (3) the NL3 region-structure/state-action contract - the orthogonal regions can never become active so "concurrent activation of different collision avoidance controls" cannot occur. These are three independent behavioral defects sharing one deterministic root cause (STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL / EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE / LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING), which I keep as one candidate per distinct contract per the instructions, using repeated facts in each candidate's basis. Cardinality contract (NL1, three regions) is handled via cardinality_bindings only, no candidate. Region-structure contract (NL3) is a structural/existence property (the three regions do exist as concurrent siblings under ActiveState) so it is satisfied structurally; I instead route the operational-consequence failure to the derived state_action contract (NL3-DERIVED) and to NL2's contracts, avoiding duplicate candidates for the same structural fact.

For obligations with a supported G1/V1 backend (i8, i9, i10, i14, i15, i16), the deterministic verdict=false directly establishes the violation with no competent rebuttal since no formal terminal edge or alternate path is supplied. For obligations lacking a frozen predicate (i0, i1, i2, i3, i4, i5, i7, i11, i12, i13), the exact source/model inventory and inspection-equivalent diagnostics still establish the same violation reading; the only alternative readings offered (e.g., 'Collision Detected' as an aggregation, narrow single-transition satisfaction, direct-child counting) are considered but are either contradicted by the model's explicit separate declaration and use of the three named events elsewhere, or are secondary/weaker readings that do not defeat the primary structural violation, so they survive only as undercutting alternatives where genuinely compatible, per the strongest_rebuttal fields supplied in each candidate.

issues.observed: Inactive -> FrontendCollision/RearEndCollision/PedestrianCollision transitions exist and are reachable, but these three target states are leaf states with zero outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING) and are dead ends; the actual mitigation regions (FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion and their BrakingControl/SteeringControl/EmergencyStop substates) are unreachable from root (STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL) because no edge connects the detection leaf states or ActiveState to those regions.
issues.reason: The NL2 contract requires the sub-machine to become active/operate the collision-avoidance mitigation upon detection; the closed model's transitions dead-end at marker states, never entering the regions that constitute the actual operating collision-avoidance behavior, so the initial-entry/activation obligation is not behaviorally realized.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The three detection transitions exist and do fire on the named events, satisfying a literal 'sub-machine responds to detection' reading if the contract is interpreted narrowly as any transition out of Inactive; the stronger 'activation as an operating scope with concurrent avoidance controls' reading is what fails.
issues.title: Detection events lead only to dead-end leaves, not to the sub-machine's operative mitigation regions

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers row for Collision_Avoided (reachable_consumer_state_refs=[], reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]) vs declared consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:12,17,22]; inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE; verify_facts.checks event-consumer:Collision_Avoided refuted.
issues.expected: Each of the three named collision-detection events must be consumed to actually trigger operating collision-avoidance behavior (entry into the corresponding mitigation region), and the resulting behavior (region activation and eventual Collision_Avoided completion) must itself be reachable and operationally closed.
issues.observed: Frontend_Collision_Detected, Rear_End_Collision_Detected, and Pedestrian_Collision_Detected each have a reachable consumer transition (transition:line:32/33/34), but that consumption only reaches a dead-end leaf state with no further behavior; the corresponding Collision_Avoided event, which is the completion signal for the mitigation regions this activation is supposed to trigger, has declared consumers (transition:line:12/17/22) but EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE -- none of its consumer transitions is reachable from root, confirming the mitigation regions those events would complete are never operationally entered.
issues.reason: NL2's activation obligation implies not just receiving the event but activating the sub-machine's operative behavior; the deterministic event-consumer facts show the completion event (Collision_Avoided) tied to the mitigation regions is declared but has zero reachable consumers, evidencing that the operational coverage this activation is supposed to establish is broken even though the initial detection transitions fire.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Each detection event's own transition is technically reachable and consumed once (satisfying a minimal event_consumption reading in isolation), so this could be read as satisfied if the contract is limited only to the detection event's own immediate transition rather than the downstream mitigation-control coverage the sub-machine's activation implies.
issues.title: Named detection events are declared-consumed but do not operationally trigger reachable mitigation-control coverage; Collision_Avoided has zero reachable consumers

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL for FrontendCollisionRegion/BrakingControl/RearEndCollisionRegion/SteeringControl/PedestrianCollisionRegion/EmergencyStop; verify_facts.checks refuted reachability rows for the same; fcstm_model.text showing no path from ActiveState/Inactive into these regions.
issues.expected: While the collision-avoidance mode is active, its three orthogonal regions (FrontendCollisionRegion/BrakingControl, RearEndCollisionRegion/SteeringControl, PedestrianCollisionRegion/EmergencyStop) must operate as ongoing concurrent behavior of the active mode.
issues.observed: All three regions and their internal control states (BrakingControl, SteeringControl, EmergencyStop) are marked STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL in the closed FCSTM; verify_facts confirms reachability refuted for each. The active mode (ActiveState) only ever reaches the Inactive/FrontendCollision/RearEndCollision/PedestrianCollision leaf states, so the regions never actually activate and no concurrent control behavior can occur.
issues.reason: This is an explicit ongoing operating-behavior obligation (concurrent activation of collision-avoidance controls) tied to state_action semantics for the active mode; since the regions realizing that behavior are unreachable, the required action cannot occur, and no frozen predicate captures this qualitative action-occurrence claim, so it is preserved as a precise W1 candidate.
issues.requirement_quote: The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The three regions are structurally declared as siblings under ActiveState with their own initial edges to BrakingControl/SteeringControl/EmergencyStop, so the structural region-and-control declaration exists; only the ongoing operational activation (reachability) is broken, which could be treated as a separate reachability defect rather than a state_action defect.
issues.title: Orthogonal regions cannot concurrently activate collision-avoidance controls because they are unreachable from root

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL rows for the three regions and their substates; verify_facts.checks refuted reachability rows (check_id reachability:state:FrontendCollisionRegion:line:9 etc.).
issues.expected: The three mitigation regions (FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion) that realize the sub-machine's collision-avoidance behavior must be reachable from the machine root once a corresponding collision is detected.
issues.observed: G1-style finite reachability fact: none of FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion (nor their BrakingControl/SteeringControl/EmergencyStop substates) is reachable from the top-level initial entry in the finite closed-model hierarchy; verify_facts explicitly refutes reachability for each.
issues.reason: This is the root/cross-wrapper reachability property distinct from the initial_entry obligation on the sub-machine itself and from the state_action obligation on ongoing concurrent behavior; G1 finite unreachable-target facts directly support it.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The regions have valid local initial edges to their controls ([*] -> BrakingControl, etc.), so locally the region-to-control entry structure is well-formed; only the cross-wrapper path from root into these regions is missing, which is a distinct global reachability defect rather than a malformed local edge.
issues.title: Collision-avoidance mitigation regions are structurally unreachable from the machine root

branches.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, and stable termination/dead-end frontier facts. The closed FCSTM shows the three collision-avoidance regions (FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion) and their internal states (BrakingControl, SteeringControl, EmergencyStop) are structurally present but entirely unreachable from the root because ActiveState's only initial edge targets Inactive, and Inactive's outgoing transitions (Frontend_Collision_Detected, Rear_End_Collision_Detected, Pedestrian_Collision_Detected) target leaf states FrontendCollision/RearEndCollision/PedestrianCollision that have zero outgoing transitions rather than entering the corresponding regions. This breaks: (1) the NL2 initial-entry/activation contract - the named collision events do not actually activate/enter the sub-machine's operative collision-handling behavior (the regions), (2) the derived NL2 event-consumer-coverage contract - Collision_Avoided has consumers but none reachable, and the named detection events lead only to dead-end leaves, not into the actual mitigation regions, (3) the NL3 region-structure/state-action contract - the orthogonal regions can never become active so "concurrent activation of different collision avoidance controls" cannot occur. These are three independent behavioral defects sharing one deterministic root cause (STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL / EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE / LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING), which I keep as one candidate per distinct contract per the instructions, using repeated facts in each candidate's basis. Cardinality contract (NL1, three regions) is handled via cardinality_bindings only, no candidate. Region-structure contract (NL3) is a structural/existence property (the three regions do exist as concurrent siblings under ActiveState) so it is satisfied structurally; I instead route the operational-consequence failure to the derived state_action contract (NL3-DERIVED) and to NL2's contracts, avoiding duplicate candidates for the same structural fact.
